code: library(hypergraphs)  # memory network: what follows what, given how you got here net <- hon(human_long, action = "code", actor = "session_id",            time = "timestamp", max_order = 3) hg_centrality(net, sort_by = "pagerank")  # simplicial complex: the same sessions as a pathway complex sc <- simplicial(net, type = "pathway") hg_betti(sc)  # hypergraph: each session as one multi-way interaction over its codes hg <- group_hypergraph(human_long, node = "code", hyperedge = "session_id") hg_centrality(hg, type = "pagerank")  # text: a corpus as a document-word hypergraph, clustered into topics thg <- text_hypergraph(covid_abstracts, column = "abstract", id = "doc",                        weight = "tfidf", stop_words = stop_words_en(),                        min_count = 3L) topics <- hg_cluster(thg, k = 4, type = "random_walk", seed = 1) hg_keywords(thg, topics, n = 5, collapse = TRUE)                    # tf-idf mass hg_keywords(thg, topics, n = 5, type = "ctfidf", collapse = TRUE)  # BERTopic's c-TF-IDF hg_keywords(thg, topics, n = 5, type = "centrality", collapse = TRUE)

eq } x_j.$$ uniform hypergraphs (hyperedges size \(k\)), equivalent normalizing ZEC update geometric-mean exponent \(1/(k-1)\). mixed sizes, effective exponent taken largest hyperedge; expect slightly different rankings ZEC mixed case. Nodes left hyperedge (possible min_weight/min_size filtering) teleport every step receive teleportation mass. undamped stationary distribution walk pi column reported hg_cluster(). Subhypergraph centrality ("subhypergraph"): logarithm diagonal matrix exponential clique adjacency derived binary incidence (entries count shared hyperedges), \(\log[\exp(W)]_{ii}\). counts closed walks based node factorial penalty length matches implementation used HypergraphX 1.5 legal-hypergraphs analysis. Katz centrality ("katz"): Katz's (1953) status index hypergraph adjacency Estrada & Rodriguez-Velazquez (2006), \(A_{ij}\) = number hyperedges containing \(\) \(j\) (weighted clique expansion), $$x = \sum_{k \ge 1} \alpha^k ^k \mathbf{1} = (- \alpha )^{-1} \alpha \mathbf{1},\qquad 0 < \alpha < 1/\lambda_{max}(),$$ \(\alpha\)-discounted number walks leaving node (Battiston et al. 2020, Sec. code: dat <- data.frame(   member = c("a", "b", "c", "b", "c", "d", "d", "e", "f"),   event = c("e1", "e1", "e1", "e2", "e2", "e2", "e3", "e3", "e4") ) hg <- group_hypergraph(dat, "member", "event") plot(hg, color_by = "size", edge_labels = TRUE)  plot(hg, detail = Inf, outline = "fill", alpha = 0.15)  plot(hg, center = c("b", "c"))  plot(hg, dismantled = TRUE)  plot(hg, type = "incidence", edge_labels = TRUE)   # tribunals in claims against Argentina, one column per tribunal by date tribunals <- group_hypergraph(icsid_tribunals, node = "arbitrator",                               hyperedge = "case") argentina <- hg_subset(tribunals,                        where = list(respondent = "Argentine Republic"),                        component = "largest") plot(argentina, type = "incidence", color_by = "economic_sector",      sort_by = "constituted")   # disconnected pieces are laid out separately and packed apart <- group_hypergraph(   data.frame(member = c("a", "b", "c", "b", "c", "d", "x", "y", "z"),              event = c("e1", "e1", "e1", "e2", "e2", "e2", "e3", "e3", "e3")),   "member", "event" ) plot(apart, color_by = "size")   # circles sized by how often each node occurs, pointing where it goes next counts <- c(a = 40, b = 25, c = 12, d = 30, e = 5, f = 2) moves <- data.frame(from = c("a", "b", "c", "d", "d", "e"),                     to = c("b", "c", "a", "e", "b", "f"),                     weight = c(20, 9, 4, 8, 3, 1)) plot(hg, node_sizes = counts, direction = moves,      size_title = "occurrences of the node")  plot(hg, node_sizes = counts, direction = moves, transitions = moves,      arrow_style = "outside")   # groups of events with their trial counts: the count colours the pebbles # and writes a title box per group; points sized by how many trials # contain each event members <- data.frame(   group = c("Hint", "Hint", "Hint", "Question", "Question", "Question"),   state = c("Wrong", "Hint", "Retry", "Wrong", "Question", "Retry"),   trials = c(120, 120, 120, 80, 80, 80) ) trial_groups <- group_hypergraph(members, node = "state", hyperedge = "group") event_trials <- data.frame(state = c("Wrong", "Hint", "Question", "Retry"),                            trials = c(200, 120, 80, 190)) plot(trial_groups, node_sizes = event_trials)

P Symmetric block--block pair probability matrix ("sbm"). block_sizes Positive integer block sizes ("sbm"). d Hyperedge size, recycled across sampled pairs; variable_size = TRUE, Poisson mean size minus two ("sbm"). impurity Number added members replaced nodes outside blocks pair ("sbm", default 0). variable_size Draw sizes 2 + Poisson(d) ("sbm", default FALSE). absolute_purity Replacements come outside blocks pair ("sbm", default TRUE). seed Optional seed; random number state caller restored exit.

title: Random hypergraphs — random_hypergraph
text: "gnp" Erdos–Renyi-style model: n nodes m hyperedges, every incidence drawn independently Bernoulli(p). m omitted Poisson mean lambda, n * p lambda also omitted. Empty singleton hyperedges retained, since outcomes model. "uniform" makes every hyperedge contain exactly k distinct nodes, "regular" makes every node belong exactly k distinct hyperedges. Sampling weights prob can unequal. "sbm" samples graph stochastic block model extends every sampled pair nodes hyperedge members blocks pair; impurity added members can replaced nodes outside blocks. type takes arguments, given name; argument chosen type take error.

code: hg <- text_hypergraph(c(   cooking_1 = "simmer the soup with onions and carrots",   cooking_2 = "this soup recipe needs salt on a cold night",   space_1 = "the telescope revealed a distant galaxy and stars",   space_2 = "astronomers aimed the telescope at the stars all night" ), stop_words = c("the", "with", "and", "a", "this", "at", "on", "all")) topics <- hg_cluster(hg, k = 2, seed = 1) topic_network(hg, clusters = topics) #>      source    target weight #> 1 Cluster 1 Cluster 2      1 topic_network(hg, clusters = topics, similarity = "cosine") #>      source    target     weight #> 1 Cluster 1 Cluster 2 0.07715167  corpus <- c(   a = "soup salt onion soup broth", b = "salt soup broth onion",   c = "stars sky moon night", d = "sky stars night moon moon",   e = "soup stars salt sky night broth", f = "onion salt stars broth") corpus_hg <- text_hypergraph(corpus) model <- hg_topics(corpus_hg, k = 2, nstart = 2) topic_network(corpus_hg, topics = model, threshold = 0.2) #>    source  target weight #> 1 Topic 1 Topic 2      1

title: Windowed Sequence Hyperedges — window_hypergraph
text: Builds hypergraph categorical sequence data: fixed-size window moves sequence distinct states observed inside one window form one hyperedge (Ding et al. 2020). Windows whose distinct state sets coincide collapse single hyperedge whose weight number windows (window_counts); incidence cells hold total within-window occurrences state, incidence matrix carries edge-dependent vertex weights (Chitra & Raphael 2019) hg_cluster() type = "random_walk" uses directly. window counts default hyperedge weights whole Laplacian family (hg_laplacian(), hg_cluster(), hg_classify()).

title: Windowed Sequence Hyperedges — window_hypergraph
code: window_hypergraph(   data,   window = 3L,   step = 1L,   action = NULL,   actor = NULL,   time = NULL,   session = NULL,   time_threshold = 900,   timezone = "UTC",   min_size = 1L,   min_weight = 1L )

title: Windowed Sequence Hyperedges — window_hypergraph
text: data Sequences form described sequence-input: long event table, wide data.frame character matrix (one sequence per row, trailing NAs stripped), list character vectors. window Integer >= 2. Window size sequence positions. step Integer >= 1. Offset consecutive window starts: 1 slides, window tumbles. action, actor, time, session, time_threshold, timezone Long-format arguments, sequence-input. min_size Integer >= 1. Drop hyperedges fewer distinct states collapsing. default 1 keeps everything. min_weight Integer >= 1. Drop hyperedges observed fewer min_weight windows, keeping recurrent state combinations (role min_freq plays rule extraction). default 1 keeps everything. total dropped min_size min_weight together recorded params$n_dropped; defaults, sum(window_counts) equals number non-empty full windows.
